bad.title: Limited Evidence-Based Validation
bad.description: Your verification practices often rely on AI self-assessment rather than independent cross-checking against original source materials. This approach can allow errors to persist undetected, as you may accept AI-generated findings without personally confirming them against the actual evidence. Strengthening your practice of returning to primary sources will significantly improve output reliability.

bad.title: Insufficient Empirical Testing of Solutions
bad.description: You tend to finalize your work without testing it in realistic conditions to see how it actually performs. This single-pass approach means you miss opportunities to discover technical errors, conceptual misalignments, or performance gaps that would only become apparent through hands-on experimentation. Testing reveals what theoretical review cannot.

bad.title: Surface-Level Conceptual Engagement
bad.description: When working with complex or ambiguous concepts, you sometimes move forward with surface understanding rather than probing deeply into distinctions, boundaries, and edge cases. This can lead to fundamental misalignments between what a task requires and what your solution delivers, even when your execution appears technically sound.

good.title: Clear Communication and Task Organization
good.description: You excel at translating your intentions into structured instructions that AI systems can understand and act upon. Your prompts are well-organized, include relevant context and examples, and successfully convey formatting requirements. This clarity in communication creates a strong foundation for productive AI collaboration and helps ensure that your requests are interpreted correctly.

good.title: Proactive Quality Control Awareness
good.description: You consistently recognize that AI outputs require verification and take steps to build validation into your workflow. Whether seeking external authoritative sources or designing creative testing approaches, you understand that blind acceptance of AI suggestions is risky. This awareness positions you well to develop more sophisticated verification practices.

good.title: Conceptual Iteration and Progressive Development
good.description: You show a willingness to build your work progressively, adding layers of detail and structure to your prompts over multiple interactions. When initial approaches don't meet your needs, you're prepared to restart and refine your strategy. This iterative mindset is essential for developing effective AI collaboration patterns.

overall.overview: Throughout this assessment, you demonstrated a **solid collaborative foundation** with clear organizational skills and good instincts for structuring interactions with AI systems. Your ability to communicate task requirements and maintain systematic workflows shows promise, and you recognize the importance of verification in AI collaboration. However, your collaboration would benefit significantly from **deeper engagement with evidence-based validation** and **iterative testing practices**—developing these areas will transform you from someone who can complete AI-assisted tasks into someone who can reliably produce high-quality, verified outputs.

improvements.title: Establish Systematic Testing Loops
improvements.description: Before finalizing any AI-assisted work, create opportunities to test your solutions with real inputs and evaluate the outputs critically. Run your prompts through actual AI systems, examine multiple results for patterns of success or failure, and use these insights to refine your approach. Testing transforms theoretical solutions into proven ones and reveals issues that review alone cannot catch.

improvements.title: Build Independent Verification Practices
improvements.description: Develop a habit of cross-referencing AI outputs directly against source materials rather than relying primarily on AI self-assessment. When the AI claims something appears in a transcript or document, locate the specific passage yourself. When it suggests an analysis, verify the reasoning against the original data. This practice builds genuine confidence in your outputs and catches errors at their source.

improvements.title: Engage Deeply with Conceptual Ambiguity
improvements.description: When encountering complex or unfamiliar concepts, resist the urge to move immediately to execution. Instead, invest time in exploring boundaries, testing edge cases, and clarifying distinctions with the AI as a thinking partner. Ask "what's the difference between X and Y?" or "what would be an example that sits on the boundary?" This deeper engagement prevents fundamental misalignments and builds more robust understanding.
